get.description:
Report whether this process can reach its database.

Unauthenticated by design and therefore returns **no more than a boolean** — no version, no
dependency list, no error detail, no tenant data. A deploy pipeline polls this to decide whether
a release actually works; a non-200 means the app is up but cannot serve, which is exactly the
failure a liveness probe cannot see.

503.description: The process cannot reach its database.

post.description:
OAuth2 compatible token login, get an access token for future requests

The account read is one statement on the autocommit engine: no `BEGIN` and no `ROLLBACK`
around it, so sign-in costs one database round trip instead of three (each ~210 ms while the
app and the database are not co-located, `docs/reference/performance.md`). The rare rehash
write commits on its own, exactly as before.

Test access token

Carries the tenant-status refusal (R10) like the other self-service routes: a suspended
organisation's session is refused here too, not only where tenant data is read.
Password Recovery

Reset password

Carries the same 5/min recovery limit as the request route
(`docs/reference/build-contract.md` control 10): the reset token is a bearer credential that
grants a session, so guessing one must be at least as expensive as asking for one. Both routes
share the `password-recovery` window, which caps recovery work from one address in total.

get.description: List the caller's organisation's accounts and the roles each holds.

post.description:
Onboard a staff member: create the account in the caller's organisation with the chosen
roles, and email them a link to set their own password.

The caller can grant only roles whose permissions they hold (R3, `403 GRANT_EXCEEDS_ACTOR`).

404.description: A role is absent, or belongs to another organisation

409.description: Refused: the address already has an account. The same answer whichever organisation holds it, so no organisation is disclosed.

503.description: Outgoing mail is not configured, so no invitation can be sent

post.description:
Resend an invitation: email a fresh link, retire the previous one and restart the window.

Checked exactly like sending one: `users:manage`, then R3 over the roles the person holds now
(`403 GRANT_EXCEEDS_ACTOR`). Only an outstanding invitation can be resent (`409`).

404.description: The account is absent, or belongs to another organisation

409.description: Refused: no invitation is outstanding (it was accepted, the person never needed one, or the account is deactivated)

503.description: Outgoing mail is not configured, so no invitation can be sent

post.description:
Register an organisation: email a link that creates it (D-008).

The answer is the same for every address. A new address is emailed a single-use link that
creates the organisation and signs its owner in; an address that already has an account is
emailed a notice instead. Nothing exists until the link is used.

503.description: Outgoing mail is not configured, so nothing is created

post.description: Send a signup's email again with a fresh link. The same answer whatever the id.
Spend a signup link: create the organisation and its owner, and sign the owner in.

400.description: The link is invalid, expired, replaced or already used

post.description: Spend an emailed invitation link: the invitee chooses their own password.

400.description: The link is invalid, expired or already used

get.description: Retrieve users.

post.description:
Create new user.

Never a superuser: that flag is set only by `FIRST_SUPERUSER` at start-up. The application role
cannot change it afterwards (migration `e1a4c7b9d2f3`), so it is not granted from an API either.

get.description: Get current user.

delete.description:
Deactivate own user.

Kept as `DELETE /users/me` for the clients that call it, but it deactivates: the account and its
attribution survive, and its next request is `401`.

get.description: Get a specific user by id.

delete.description:
Deactivate a user.

Administered offboarding, answered with the route's existing `DELETE` verb: R14, and the reason
the foreign keys on `user_roles` are `ON DELETE RESTRICT`. Nothing is removed from the database —
the account, its grants and its audit attribution stay — and the account's next request is `401`.

post.description: Test emails.
Create a contact in the caller's workspace. The workspace comes from the session.

get.description: One keyset page of the workspace's contacts. Follow `next_cursor` for the next page.

post.description: Find contacts by name or email prefix, exact phone number, or `#tag`. Keyset-paged.

get.description: One contact. Another workspace's contact is `404`.

patch.description: Change the fields sent; the rest are left alone.

post.description: Record a WhatsApp opt-in or opt-out, and how it was given.
Block (no new bookings), archive (leaves the list) or reactivate a contact.

get.description: List the organisation's roles with each role's permission bundle.
List the global permission catalogue (read-only reference data; R7).
The caller's own effective permission codes. Advisory UI data; never a control.
List the roles one account of the caller's tenant holds. Another tenant's account is `404`.

post.description:
Grant a role to an account. `201` when created, `200` when the account already holds it.

The grantability rule (R3) is applied in the service before the row is written: a bundle
containing a permission the caller does not hold is refused `403 GRANT_EXCEEDS_ACTOR`.

200.description: The account already held the role; nothing was written

get.description: The effective permission set of one account, computed server-side. Cross-tenant is `404`.

delete.description:
Revoke a role from an account. The delete is real; the audit trail is the history.

R8: the removal that would leave the organisation with nobody holding `users:manage` is refused
`409 LAST_ADMINISTRATOR` and nothing is removed.

409.description: Refused: this is the organisation's last role granting `users:manage` (R8). Assign another administrator first.

get.description: Return the caller's own tenant. `retention_profile` is never part of the answer (US-1).

patch.description:
Refuse a tenant security-setting change: the required step-up control is not built (R12).

The body has already been validated by the time this runs — `TenantSettingsUpdate` declares no
field and forbids extras, so a body `tenant_id` or any other name is a `422` from the validation
layer and never reaches this function. What remains is the authorisation decision and the refusal
that the missing step-up forces; the declaration on this module records why no success path exists
and what the writer must emit when it does.

403.description: Refused. `PERMISSION_NOT_HELD` when the caller does not hold `tenant:configure`; `STEP_UP_REQUIRED` for a caller who does, because the step-up control this route requires is not built (feature 02, blocked by D-003). Nothing is written.

get.description:
The caller's own clinic's display name, for every member of it.

No permission code: the display name is PUBLIC (the booking page shows it to anyone), and the
route answers only for the session's own organisation. An account with no organisation, or one
whose organisation is not active, is refused by `get_actor` before this runs.

patch.description:
Rename the caller's own clinic (Practice Owner). Audited on the same transaction.

The body is validated first (a blank, over-long or unprintable name is a `422`), then the
permission is decided; a refusal is audited before it is raised.

403.description: `PERMISSION_NOT_HELD`: renaming the clinic needs `tenant:configure`. Audited `tenant.config_changed` `DENIED`; nothing is changed.

get.description: One keyset page of the caller's audit trail, newest first, and the read is itself audited.
One event of the caller's trail. Another tenant's event is `404`, and the attempt is audited.
Bookable staff: active accounts holding a Doctor, Authorised Prescriber or Nurse role.
Appointments starting in `[from, to)`, at most 31 days, earliest first.

409.description: Refused by the booking rules (overlap, slot taken, illegal transition)

post.description:
Book a contact with a practitioner. `409 APPOINTMENT_OVERLAP` names the clash's time.

The contact's confirmation email is sent after the booking commits (when email is configured).

409.description: Refused by the booking rules (overlap, slot taken, illegal transition)

post.description: Move a booking through its states. `409 ILLEGAL_STATE_TRANSITION` outside R4's table.

409.description: Refused by the booking rules (overlap, slot taken, illegal transition)

get.description: One contact's bookings, newest first. Another workspace's contact is `404`.

409.description: Refused by the booking rules (overlap, slot taken, illegal transition)

get.description:
The clinic's public display name, for the booking page's heading. Unauthenticated.

Only the PUBLIC display name: never `legal_name`, the tenant id or the status. Resolved like the
other public routes (only an `ACTIVE` clinic; anything else is the same `404 WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND`).

404.description: No such clinic, or not taking bookings

get.description: Free slots for one visit type over the next 14 days. Unauthenticated.

404.description: No such clinic, or not taking bookings

post.description: Book from the public page. The same answer whether the contact was new or already known.

404.description: No such clinic, or not taking bookings

get.description: The clinic's hours and slot length, for every member: opening hours are PUBLIC.

put.description: Set the hours per weekday and the slot length (Practice Owner). Audited on its transaction.

403.description: `PERMISSION_NOT_HELD`: changing the hours needs `tenant:configure`. Audited; nothing changes.

post.description:
Send every due booking confirmation and reminder, one tenant at a time. Counts only.

For a scheduler (D-009). No tenant is named by the caller: the job reads the active tenants and
runs each in its own transaction. Idempotent: a second call sends nothing the first one sent.

404.description: The job endpoint is not enabled on this server

post.description:
Re-prove the factor (interim: the password, ADR-F002) for one operation on one resource.

`docs/features/02-authentication/03-design.md` names this route (`POST /api/v1/auth/step-up`,
*"issue a single-use resource-bound step-up token"*). The grant lives two minutes, is bound to this
account, the operation and the resource id, and is spent by the operation's own transaction. No
permission is checked here: the grant authorises nothing by itself, and the operation that spends
it checks its own permission first. A wrong password answers `403`, never `401`, so the client
does not sign the clinician out for a typo.

403.description: `STEP_UP_FAILED`: the password did not verify. Audited; nothing issued.

get.description: The setup checklist for whoever configures the workspace (`workspace:configure`).
The workspace settings (`workspace:read`); the defaults when none were saved.

patch.description:
Save the workspace settings (`workspace:configure`).
Audited `tenant.config_changed` with the names of the fields that changed.

AppointmentCreate.title: AppointmentCreate
AppointmentCreate.description: `POST /appointments`. The server computes `ends_at` from the type (R2).

AppointmentSettingsRead.title: AppointmentSettingsRead
AppointmentSettingsRead.description: `GET /appointment-settings`: the slot length and seven days of hours, Monday first.

AppointmentSettingsSaved.title: AppointmentSettingsSaved
AppointmentSettingsSaved.description:
`PUT /appointment-settings`: the saved settings, and how many upcoming live bookings now fall
outside the hours. Those bookings are kept; the count lets the screen say so.

AppointmentSettingsUpdate.title: AppointmentSettingsUpdate
AppointmentSettingsUpdate.description: `PUT /appointment-settings`. Strict; every rule is a `422` naming the day it is about.

AuditEventRead.title: AuditEventRead
AuditEventRead.description:
One audit event as the API returns it — the design's envelope, and nothing else.

`tenant_id` is not declared: the caller already knows its own tenant, and the row was read under
it. `prev_hash` and `hash` are exposed because verifying the trail is the point of reading it.

AuditEventsPublic.title: AuditEventsPublic
AuditEventsPublic.description:
A keyset page of audit events.

`next_cursor` is opaque and `None` on the last page. `count` is the number of rows in this page,
not the tenant's total: the total is not disclosed and is not knowable without a scan, which R12
refuses.

ContactOptIn.title: ContactOptIn
ContactOptIn.description: `POST /contacts/{id}/opt-in`: record a WhatsApp opt-in or opt-out, and how it was given.

ContactSearch.title: ContactSearch
ContactSearch.description: `POST /contacts/search`. A body, not a URL, so a name or number never lands in a log line.

DayHours-Input.title: DayHours
DayHours-Input.description: One weekday's hours. Closed is both times `null`.

DayHours-Output.title: DayHours
DayHours-Output.description: One weekday's hours. Closed is both times `null`.

InvitationAccept.title: InvitationAccept
InvitationAccept.description:
The body of `POST /api/v1/users/invitations/accept`: the emailed token and a new password.

The password bounds are the API's own (`UserRegister`, `NewPassword`): 8 to 128 characters.

InvitationAccepted.title: InvitationAccepted
InvitationAccepted.description: The account the invitation belonged to, so the app can sign the person straight in.

NotificationRunReport.title: NotificationRunReport
NotificationRunReport.description: What one run of the booking-email job did, in counts only.

OrganisationSignup.title: OrganisationSignup
OrganisationSignup.description:
The body of `POST /api/v1/users/signup` (D-008). Strict: any other key is `422`.

The field rules are the ones `UserRegister` had (password 8 to 128 characters, the rest at most
255). `workspace_name` registers an organisation; without it the account belongs to none, which is
what a platform administrator registers.

OwnPermissionsRead.title: OwnPermissionsRead
OwnPermissionsRead.description:
The caller's own effective permission codes, sorted (`GET /api/v1/users/me/permissions`).

Advisory UI data: the shell reads it to hide controls a role cannot use. It is the design's
self-permissions row (`03-design.md`, "Endpoints": *"advisory UI data only; never a
control"*). Every route still re-authorises
server-side (INV-3). No user or tenant identifier is echoed back: the caller is the session.

PermissionRead.title: PermissionRead
PermissionRead.description:
One entry of the global permission catalogue.

`permissions.id` is not exposed: `code` is the catalogue's stable identity and the join key is
internal. `permissions` is global read-only reference data (R7).

PermissionsPublic.title: PermissionsPublic
PermissionsPublic.description: The permission catalogue, or a computed subset of it, plus its size.

PractitionerRead.title: PractitionerRead
PractitionerRead.description:
A bookable member of staff: an active account holding a Doctor, Authorised Prescriber or
Nurse role in the session's organisation.

PublicBookingCreated.title: PublicBookingCreated
PublicBookingCreated.description: The confirmation. The same shape whether the contact was new or matched (never says which).

PublicBookingRequest.title: PublicBookingRequest
PublicBookingRequest.description: `POST /public/{workspace_slug}/bookings`: a slot, who the contact is, and the APP 5 consent.

PublicSlot.title: PublicSlot
PublicSlot.description: One free, bookable time. Only what the booking page shows: never another contact's data.

PublicWorkspaceRead.title: PublicWorkspaceRead
PublicWorkspaceRead.description: `GET /api/v1/public/{workspace_slug}`: all an unauthenticated visitor learns about a clinic.

RoleAssignmentCreate.title: RoleAssignmentCreate
RoleAssignmentCreate.description:
The body of `POST /api/v1/users/{user_id}/roles`.

Only `role_id` is accepted. A `tenant_id` (INV-1), a `granted_by` or a `user_id` is an unknown
field and is rejected `422` before any query runs — the design's step 5 names exactly those three.

RoleRead.title: RoleRead
RoleRead.description: A tenant-scoped role and the permission bundle it resolves to.

RolesPublic.title: RolesPublic
RolesPublic.description: The organisation's roles, ordered by code, plus their count.

SetupRead.title: SetupRead
SetupRead.description: The setup checklist (R1-R3), every step derived from live data.

SignupAccepted.title: SignupAccepted
SignupAccepted.description:
The one answer to a signup, whatever the address: this attempt's id and the link's window.

`request_id` identifies the attempt (for "Send the email again"), never an account.

SignupVerify.title: SignupVerify
SignupVerify.description: The body of `POST /api/v1/users/signup/verify`: the emailed token, only ever in a body.

StaffInvitationRead.title: StaffInvitationRead
StaffInvitationRead.description:
An outstanding invitation: when the current link was sent and when it stops working.

`expired` is decided by the server's clock, so a screen never has to trust the device's.

StaffInvite.title: StaffInvite
StaffInvite.description:
The body of `POST /api/v1/users/staff`: who to invite and the role(s) they start with.

Strict (`extra="forbid"`) for every key but one. **A `tenant_id` is ignored and audited** rather
than refused (INV-1: *"a `tenant_id` from a body, header or query parameter is ignored and audited
as a cross-tenant attempt"*): the wrap validator drops it before validation and records that it
was there, and the service writes the audit event in the invitation's own transaction. The
invitation always lands in the session's tenant. There is no password field: the invitee
chooses their own through the emailed link.

StaffMemberRead.title: StaffMemberRead
StaffMemberRead.description:
One account of the caller's organisation (`GET`/`POST /api/v1/users/staff`).

No `tenant_id` (the caller's own), no `is_superuser` (a platform attribute an organisation does
not administer) and no credential material. `invitation` is present only while the status is
`INVITED`.

StaffPublic.title: StaffPublic
StaffPublic.description: One page of the organisation's staff, plus the organisation's total.

StaffRoleRead.title: StaffRoleRead
StaffRoleRead.description: One role a staff member holds: enough to show and to address it, not its bundle.

StepUpGrantRead.title: StepUpGrantRead
StepUpGrantRead.description: The single-use proof. `step_up_token` is SECRET: held by the client for one call, never logged.

StepUpRequest.title: StepUpRequest
StepUpRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/auth/step-up`: re-prove the session's factor for one operation on one resource.

The interim factor is the account password (ADR-F002; D-003 decides the real one). `operation`
is a closed vocabulary and `resource_id` is the record the operation will act on, so the grant
this returns cannot be spent on anything else. No `user_id` or `tenant_id`: both are the session.

TenantCurrentRead.title: TenantCurrentRead
TenantCurrentRead.description:
The caller's own tenant, as `GET /api/v1/workspaces/current` returns it.

`status` and `data_region` are shown (US-1). `retention_profile` and `legal_name` are not: the
application role holds no `SELECT` on either (`03-design.md`, "Database privileges").

TenantProfileRead.title: TenantProfileRead
TenantProfileRead.description: The caller's own clinic as every member of it may see it: the PUBLIC display name only.

TenantProfileUpdate.title: TenantProfileUpdate
TenantProfileUpdate.description:
The body of `PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/current/profile`.

Strict (`extra="forbid"`): any unknown key is a `422`. The one exception is `tenant_id`, which
INV-1 says is **ignored and audited** rather than refused: it is dropped before validation and the
service records the attempt on the change's own transaction.

TenantSettingsUpdate.title: TenantSettingsUpdate
TenantSettingsUpdate.description:
The body of `PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/current` — no field is settable yet.

`extra="forbid"` is what makes that a control rather than a comment: a client cannot smuggle a
`tenant_id` (or any future setting) past the route, and any name it sends is a `422` decided by the
validation layer, in the same order the design fixes (validate against a strict schema).

UserPermissionsRead.title: UserPermissionsRead
UserPermissionsRead.description:
The effective permission set of one account, computed server-side from its roles.

The design names this "effective set, computed server-side": nothing here comes from the request,
and the set is the union of the account's role bundles (R1).

UserRoleRead.title: UserRoleRead
UserRoleRead.description:
One role an account holds inside the caller's tenant.

`granted_at` is returned because an access review needs the age of the grant (US-2); the granter's
identifier is not.

UserRolesPublic.title: UserRolesPublic
UserRolesPublic.description: The roles one account holds, plus their count.
